tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

- **Derivation:** 5 requirements, every cited ID exists, all have evidence (2–9 verbatims each); spot-checked citations support the claims. Weak points: all 5 tagged `at_successor_launch`, 4/5 Kano `basic`; metrics have no numeric targets (model says so in assumptions); 2 requirements rest on 2–3 verbatims, expected at n=50.

- Feedback types: like 2,777 · complaint 851 · want 699 · defect 580 · difficult_to_use 493.
- Top categories: Infotainment & Digital 1,023 · Driving Experience 901 · Comfort & Space 781 · Interior 572 · Exterior 550.
- 33 signals (0.6%) have unverified quotes — mostly stitched with "…" or a changed word form ("enjoy" vs "enjoys"); flagged, not dropped.

- 11 calls, **$0.1342** (agent had estimated ≈ $0.05 — off by 2.7×: sol output 1.2–2k tokens/call at $5/M Flex). Avg 3.4k in / 1.6k out per call.

- **111 of 268 flipped to in scope, 157 confirmed out of scope; 118 new signals**, 0 unverified quotes, 0 missing IDs.
- New signals: difficult_to_use 80 (66 of them hotline questions like "customer asked which regen setting to use"), like 17, defect 12, complaint 5, want 4. Real recoveries include "only fast charged to 80%, which i really hated", a flat-tire defect, oil-dipstick want, removed gesture control. The question-type ones are a looser rule than the first pass applied → Q-020.

## Risks / watch-outs

- Local anaconda Python 3.9 has a broken pandas/numpy → use `uv venv --python 3.12`.
- Option lists are German-market only — the US/CN equipment baseline is an assumption.
- Plant capacity/flexibility is rarely public → feasibility checks need explicit assumptions (Q-011).
- BMW says engineering is out of scope → keep feasibility framed as a filter (Q-010).
- BMW data must never be committed or sent anywhere except OpenAI (AGENTS rule 1).
- Public sales are only in model-series pairs, with no regional per-model figures. Model-level market volume relies on BMW's `sales_volumes.xlsx`, which looks stylized and conflicts with public China data (Q-015).
- Scoring as drafted penalizes CN (no verbatims) and G70 EU (~19 verbatims) — see Q-004.
- Feedback data has no dates → the 2-year process must be demoed as simulated ingest waves (Q-012).
- `gpt-6-luna` structured-output quality is untested → pilot first (D-014); fallback `gpt-5-mini`.
- China-built i5 (G68 BEV) reportedly ended Jul 2026 (insider rumour, unconfirmed by BMW as of 2026-10-10) — affects 5 Series China powertrain assumptions.
- X5/7 Series successors: BMW calls them NK models, trade press says the platform is CLAR-derived (`bmw-annual-report-2025.md` §4). This matters for the G70 successor.

## Session log

- 2026-10-10 — Foundation created: challenge analysis, data inventory, proposed stack/architecture, agent rules.
## D-040 — Two real-date checkpoints instead of simulated waves; checkpoint research layer
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("divide a year into 2 … randomly apply all the customer feedback into those two … if we know it for sure because it is posted on the internet, use realistic data … Jan 2026 and Jul 2026"; "forget everything we already implemented"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted for the research layer; how classification, clustering, contextualizing and requirement elicitation use it is left to Atahan's next steps · Supersedes D-027's wave definitions once integrated.
- Context: D-027 simulated time with a random 50/50 split plus an invented "market event" wave dated 2026-11 to 2027-11. Atahan questioned why waves exist at all and asked for real, dated public evidence so the effect of time on AI proposals is visible.
- Decision:
  1. **Two checkpoints** = what a PM could know on **31 Jan 2026** (FY2025 results) and **31 Jul 2026** (H1 2026 results). An item belongs to the earliest checkpoint whose cut-off is ≥ its source publication date; nothing published after 31 Jul 2026 is used. Month-only dates count as month end; undated history pages (predecessor background) count as known at Jan and are flagged `undated`.
  2. **Customer feedback** (no dates) keeps the stratified 50/50 split of D-027 (seed 2026): half visible at Jan, all at Jul.
  3. **Research layer** `research/checkpoints/`: `SCHEMA.md` (item schema, trust tiers, pairing rule), `raw/<topic>.json` from 8 research agents (markets, BMW portfolio + predecessors G30/G11/F40, premium competitors, EV challengers, segment sales, tech trends, policy & macro, consumer studies), merged and validated by `scripts/checkpoints_merge.py` → `checkpoints.json` (821 items, 778 quotes checked on the page, 299 metric pairs across both checkpoints; T1 369 / T2 323 / T3 129). Public web data only, so it is committed.
  4. **Comparisons use year-on-year change and shares**, never absolute volumes (full year vs half year). When a figure has no Jul update, the Jan value is shown as "old", not dropped.
  5. **Checkpoint Atlas** (`scripts/checkpoints_page.py` → `atlas.html`, a local page; not published) visualises the layer with a two-step Jan/Jul switch bottom-right; every mark opens its source.
- Consequences: research gaps tracked in Q-026. The pipeline still runs on the D-027 waves until Atahan leads the classification → clustering → contextualization → elicitation rebuild.

## D-041 — Checkpoint lineage, comment galaxy and a new 3D frontend
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("design a black bg app with minimal design philosophy … graphic and 3D … make sure the second checkpoint will work on the output of checkpoint 1 and recalibrate requirements with the newly added data"; chose: comment galaxy as the first view, all BMW-internal data known at Jan, replace the old app, direction "track-while-scan"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted · Implements D-040; supersedes D-027's wave definitions and the D-039 screens.
- Decision:
  1. **Schema:** `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_run` (stage, parent_run_id), `track` (new/held/strengthened/weakened/lost with weight and prev_weight), `source_layout`; `source_item.checkpoint`. Module `bmw_req/checkpoints.py`: visibility rules, research import (`research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json` → `source_item(kind=research)`, 1,028 items), `start_run` refuses a cp2 run without a completed cp1 run of the same stage, `write_tracks` computes states against the parent and writes `lost` rows explicitly. Stage `acquire` run at both checkpoints (cp2: 6,645 held, 5,610 new). Tests: `tests/test_checkpoints.py`.
  2. **Galaxy:** all 10,128 raw comments embedded with text-embedding-3-small ($0.009) and laid out once in 3D (`bmw_req/pipeline/galaxy.py`); no AI interpretation of the text.
  3. **Frontend:** the D-039 screens and components are deleted; new app = checkpoint provider + sweep control + Scan screen (React + react-three-fiber, same stack). Colour encodes track state (blue = acquired by this sweep, white = held), not categories; isolation by car/market/channel/label/engine via the key.
- Consequences: the old API endpoints stay until the new screens replace them; their tests assume the 3-wave demo DB (3 fail on the current wave-1 DB, unrelated to this change). The calibration lab (`web/lab.html`, `web/src/three`) is kept.

## D-042 — One 5 Series; car rings carry dated public data
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("merge them into one 5 Series sector"; chose "add public July data" for the static rings), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Context: G68 has no comments and no own sales row (BMW's sheet is one G60_G68 tab); as its own car it was a near-empty sector. Study, options and sales rings never changed at JUL because BMW's files exist once (all known at JAN, D-041).
- Decision:
  1. **The 5 Series is one car line.** Requirements belong to the line; the China target is realised on the G68 (`market_variant`), US/EU on the G60. The G68 stays a separate vehicle in the data. On the scan: three car sectors; the last ~28 % of the 5 Series sector is the "LWB · China" part (G68 study items and sales, China research).
  2. **Car-specific public research goes onto the car's rings** (`api/routers/scan.py: research_cars / research_ring`): sales metrics → sales ring (stem = public volume), studies/reviews/awards → study ring, product news → options ring. They are contacts like the comments (dot = held, ring = acquired at JUL, flare when the sweep passes), drawn beside BMW's own marks and never blended with them (Q-015). The date ring keeps the remaining research and moved inside, next to the comments.
- Consequences: at JUL every ring gains items (public H1 2026 sales, J.D. Power 2026 IQS/APEAL awards, ADAC 2026, the 7 Series facelift and i7-China news). Matching is a regex on entity/headline; items naming BMW as a whole are matched by headline.

## D-043 — Structure & context: classify → cluster → contextualize → elicit, per checkpoint
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan (fresh extraction; evidence graph in SQLite with RAG; page 2 "collapse into structure"; "spawn sub agents to find optimizations … I want to see improvements with the new data"), designed from three read-only reviews (classification, clustering, contextualize), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Decision (code in `src/bmw_req/structure/`, every stage a `checkpoint_run`; cp2 builds on cp1):
  1. **classify** (`classify.py`, extract-v4): fixed ~45-aspect taxonomy shared by all sources (`taxonomy.py`); intensity (1–3) separate from impact; nature/want_kind/occupant/context/benchmark/future_cue/explicit; one signal per (aspect, nature); hints for Source C self-reported severity and the Source D survey prompt (never quoted); quotes ≥ 4 words; ~2.6k-token cacheable prompt; 20 comments per luna Flex call. cp2 classifies only the delta. A/B on a fixed 400-comment sample (`scripts/benchmark_classify.py`, `data/eval/classify_ab.json`): BMW-label macro 0.609 → 0.615, likes 0.84 → 0.90, "serious" → high 0.17 → 0.37, "minor" → low 0.22 → 0.49, quotes < 4 words 13 % → 5 %, survey-prompt quotes 10 → 0, Korea in-scope 0.71 → 0.76, aspect coverage 0 → 99 %; wants 0.56 → 0.54 (≈). `classify_context.py`: study rows (|z| ≥ 0.8 → gap/like), research (luna: aspect + nature), options (aspect) into `source_aspect`.
  2. **cluster** (`cluster.py`): portfolio-wide within polarity × category, average linkage 0.35 + recursive split of oversized clusters; stable keys `cl:<pol>:<cat>:<anchor>`; cp2 assigns new signals to cp1 clusters (mean-member cosine ≤ 0.35), clusters only leftovers; track weight = comment share, strengthened/weakened only if ≥ 10 % relative AND |z| ≥ 1.96 (the random JAN/JUL split must not look like change).
  3. **contextualize** (`contextualize.py`): luna standardizes one insight per cluster (title, statement, need type, quality issue, product decision); duplicate judge on cosine ≥ 0.86 pairs; themes (average linkage 0.45 on statement embeddings, cp2 joins nearest cp1 theme ≥ 0.55); RAG: research/study/options embedded once (`node_embedding`), per theme top-k checkpoint-visible candidates verified by luna into typed `evidence_edge`s (supports, contradicts, competes_with, trend_for, available_as_option, context). cp2 re-runs only changed clusters/themes; clean ones carry their edges as held.
  4. **areas** (`areas.py`): this step structures, it does not draft requirements (Atahan: drafting proposals is the next step). sol groups the themes into 15–40 potential requirement areas (title, need, kind improve / keep / emerging, why now from the given evidence, ≤ 3 open questions for drafting); code adds comments, line × market coverage and evidence counts; quality-only themes form a separate quality list. cp2 keeps area keys, attaches new themes, records change notes; tracks significance-tested. `elicit.py` (candidate drafting with code checks: future horizon needs a dated trend edge, own-market evidence per target, cited ids from the theme's edges) is kept for the next step and not run here.
  5. **Page 2 "Structure"** (`/structure`, same canvas as the scan): comments morph into their clusters; cluster nodes (blue improve / white keep; dot held, ring new, double ring strengthened, amber weakened/lost), theme halos, requirement-area diamonds above their themes, evidence arcs to the exact ring items; stage funnel; live agent panel (stages, progress, feed of AI steps from the audit trail; comments flash as they are classified); inspectors for clusters (signals with quotes), themes (evidence by relation) and areas (need, why now, open questions, coverage); "What the AI found" on comments and research on page 1. API `api/routers/structure.py`.
- Consequences: the old pipeline (`pipeline/`, extract-v3, findings, requirements, linker) stays for history but the new screens read only D-043 tables. Q-021 (over-linking) and the D-038 defect rule are enforced in code here.

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Stack

React + TypeScript (Vite) frontend with three.js via react-three-fiber for real-time 3D; a small FastAPI JSON layer (`api/`) over the existing Python pipeline (`src/bmw_req`, SQLite). Chosen by Atahan on 2026-10-11 to replace the Streamlit UI (D-039). Runs locally only (confidential BMW data, AGENTS rule 1).

## Users

- **Primary: a BMW product manager (PM)** responsible for what the successor of a car line (1, 5, 7 Series) offers its customers in each market. Over a ~2-year process they review AI-drafted customer requirements, decide (approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge, always with a reason), set priorities per car × market, and hand the result to engineering — while new evidence keeps arriving.
- **Demo audience: BMW judges and mentors** of the "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon, watching the PM (Atahan) work the tool live on a laptop or projector. The UI is tuned demo-first: the story must land in a few clicks, without breaking the real tool underneath.

## Product Purpose

Turn ~10k customer comments, a customer study, sales data, option lists and cited web research into prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements for successor BMW cars, per car and market. The AI reads, groups, drafts, checks fit and scores; the PM decides; everything is traceable to the customer's words and audited. Success: a PM trusts and acts on the ranking because every number explains itself, and the judges see a living decision process, not a one-shot list.

## Positioning

Not a feedback dashboard and not a chatbot: a decision instrument. Every requirement is a product decision BMW could take or trade off, scored per market with a visible factor breakdown, traced down to individual comments, gated by brand fit, and re-proposed — never silently changed — as new evidence arrives in waves.

## Operating Context

- Simulated ~2-year process: three evidence waves (feedback has no dates), each re-scoring and producing AI change proposals the PM accepts or rejects.
- Portfolio: F70 (1 Series), G60 (5 Series), G68 (5 Series LWB, China), G70 (7 Series); markets USA, Europe, China, Rest of world.
- Hand-offs: defect-type pain goes to a Quality hand-over list, not into requirements; the approved list is exported.
- Today's car matters as a reference: the current car and its equipment (German price list; public BMW configurator) are the baseline the successor improves on.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- AI only proposes; approved/rejected/deferred need a named human and a rationale. Brand-fit FAIL blocks approval unless the PM overrides with a reason. Audit is append-only.
- Scope: customer-facing requirements only — no regulatory, engineering specs or pricing.
- Evidence and assumption are always shown apart; conflicting evidence is surfaced, not hidden; markets without own comments are labelled.
- OpenAI is the only LLM provider; $100 total budget; running a wave costs money and takes minutes.
- Terminology to keep (English): Must / Should / Could; "5 Series · USA"; Strong / Good / Limited evidence / Assumption only; Expected / Differentiator / Delighter; To review / Challenged / Approved / Deferred / Rejected; "AI suggests" for unconfirmed priorities.

## D-048 — Requirement definition: measurable ladders, coupled requirements, shown on the car
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("go ahead, i agree" to the proposal: ladder with PM choosing, 1–3 requirements per area, links feed prioritization as bundles/flags/enabler credit without automatic penalties, ≤ $0.5 gap research); implemented by agents · Status: accepted · Builds on D-043 (areas), D-038 (one product decision, one metric), D-012 (future horizon), D-046 (market weights). Contract: `documents/requirement-definition.md`.
- Context: BMW's reference process step 3 asks for specification & quantification ("Range: 600 or 700 mi?", "Cooler for how many bottles?", "Seat ventilation: fast enough?"), grouped by Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver assistance. `elicit.py` (never run) had metric names but no values, no acceptance criteria, no benchmarks and no links; cited numbers existed only as free text.
- Decision:
  1. **Areas are BMW's step 2** ("potential requirements, 0/1"); the new layer drafts **1–3 requirements per non-quality area** (`define`, sol), each one product decision.
  2. **`specify`**: one customer-experienced metric (no component specs — scope), ≤ 4 acceptance criteria with market conditions, and a **target ladder per line × market**: baseline (today's BMW) → threshold (competitive parity) → target (projected to launch) → stretch (delighter). Every level has a basis `cited | projected | assumption | gap`; code downgrades unverifiable citations and never fills a gap with an invented number. The AI recommends a rung; **the PM chooses** (append-only `def_choice` + audit).
  3. **`benchmarks`**: a `spec_fact` table of cited numeric facts (attribute, value, unit, cycle, entity, source) extracted with luna from research / web / reference items, plus one capped gap-research round (≤ $0.5). Visibility follows the source's checkpoint, so a competitor raising the bar between JAN and JUL moves the ladder at cp2.
  4. **`couple`**: requirement links `conflicts | competes_for | enables | synergy` with a **via** resource (energy, mass, thermal, package, attention, aero, acoustic, compute). Candidates come deterministically from shared resources (`definition/domains.py`), luna judges, sol re-checks strong/conflict links. Links are proposals; the PM confirms/removes/adds (`def_link_review`). Relational table, no graph DB (D-017).
  5. **Domains and car zones are config** derived from aspects (`definition/domains.py`), never chosen by the LLM; zone `underfloor` (battery & energy) added to `car_zones.ZONES`.
  6. **Prioritization (next layer)** uses links as bundles (strong components prioritized together), conflict flags between Musts ("choose ladder levels jointly") and enabler credit — no automatic score penalties from conflicts.
  7. **Page 3 "Definition"**: requirement pins on the 3D car by zone, coloured by domain; selecting one flies to its zone and shows the ladder; links are drawn as arcs through the car labelled with the via.
- Consequences: planned spend ≈ $3–4 for both checkpoints (pilot first). The old `requirement` tables stay for history. Open: scoring rebuild on `def_requirement` (prioritization layer).

# Product
<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->
## Platform
web
## Stack
React + TypeScript (Vite) frontend with three.js via react-three-fiber for real-time 3D; a small FastAPI JSON layer (`api/`) over the existing Python pipeline (`src/bmw_req`, SQLite). Chosen by Atahan on 2026-10-11 to replace the Streamlit UI (D-039). Runs locally only (confidential BMW data, AGENTS rule 1).
## Users
- **Primary: a BMW product manager (PM)** responsible for what the successor of a car line (1, 5, 7 Series) offers its customers in each market. Over a ~2-year process they review AI-drafted customer requirements, decide (approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge, always with a reason), set priorities per car × market, and hand the result to engineering — while new evidence keeps arriving.
- **Demo audience: BMW judges and mentors** of the "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon, watching the PM (Atahan) work the tool live on a laptop or projector. The UI is tuned demo-first: the story must land in a few clicks, without breaking the real tool underneath.
## Product Purpose
Turn ~10k customer comments, a customer study, sales data, option lists and cited web research into prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements for successor BMW cars, per car and market. The AI reads, groups, drafts, checks fit and scores; the PM decides; everything is traceable to the customer's words and audited. Success: a PM trusts and acts on the ranking because every number explains itself, and the judges see a living decision process, not a one-shot list.
## Positioning
Not a feedback dashboard and not a chatbot: a decision instrument. Every requirement is a product decision BMW could take or trade off, scored per market with a visible factor breakdown, traced down to individual comments, gated by brand fit, and re-proposed — never silently changed — as new evidence arrives in waves.
## Operating Context
- Simulated ~2-year process: three evidence waves (feedback has no dates), each re-scoring and producing AI change proposals the PM accepts or rejects.
- Portfolio: F70 (1 Series), G60 (5 Series), G68 (5 Series LWB, China), G70 (7 Series); markets USA, Europe, China, Rest of world.
- Hand-offs: defect-type pain goes to a Quality hand-over list, not into requirements; the approved list is exported.
- Today's car matters as a reference: the current car and its equipment (German price list; public BMW configurator) are the baseline the successor improves on.
## Capabilities and Constraints
- AI only proposes; approved/rejected/deferred need a named human and a rationale. Brand-fit FAIL blocks approval unless the PM overrides with a reason. Audit is append-only.
- Scope: customer-facing requirements only — no regulatory, engineering specs or pricing.
- Evidence and assumption are always shown apart; conflicting evidence is surfaced, not hidden; markets without own comments are labelled.
- OpenAI is the only LLM provider; $100 total budget; running a wave costs money and takes minutes.
- Terminology to keep (English): Must / Should / Could; "5 Series · USA"; Strong / Good / Limited evidence / Assumption only; Expected / Differentiator / Delighter; To review / Challenged / Approved / Deferred / Rejected; "AI suggests" for unconfirmed priorities.
- A parallel workstream (D-040+) adds requirement origins (competitors, trends, regulation, personas), a regulatory radar, customer & model groups, an offering matrix per market and market intelligence; the IA must have a home for these.
## Brand Commitments
- English UI, current domain terms.
- Dark theme only.
- A BMW-like blue accent is wanted.
- No BMW logo or trademark branding in the UI; neutral product name.
## Evidence on Hand
- Live demo database `data/app.db` (39 requirements, 151 car × market targets, 3 runs, ~1.6k audit events, findings, signals with verbatim quotes, study metrics, sales, option lists, 219 cited web items). Verbatims are BMW-confidential: localhost only.
- 3D models of today's cars: public CC BY Sketchfab models (attribution required), downloaded by Atahan into `data/models/` (Q-025). Fan-made approximations, not BMW CAD.
- No testimonials, user research or production usage exist — never fabricate them.
## Product Principles
1. The PM decides, the AI explains — every AI output is a proposal with its cause visible.
2. One number, fully opened — any score can be unfolded to its factors and down to the customer's words.
3. Markets are different customers — never average them away; show where they disagree.
4. The car is the canvas — requirements are about a physical product; show them on it.

The logo is a great white's head seen straight from the side, abstracted to a single geometric line (dome to the snout tip, a straight mouth cut, the lower jaw), traced from a reference photo Atahan supplied (`web/src/components/Logo.tsx`, `web/public/favicon.svg`). - Consequences: the wordmark sits left of the page tabs at top centre; the top-bar pills (Evidence, Structure, Audit) grew from 28 to 32px, 13px text, to carry it. The localStorage key `successor.actor` is kept so the saved PM actor survives the rename.

  1. **BMW's sales file = relative weight only**: share of BMW's 2025 volume per car line × market (G60 + G68 summed), always labelled "internal and stylized (Q-015)". Its growth is never used as a trend.
  2. **Trends only from cited public research items** visible at the checkpoint: latest year-over-year change per line × market with source id, period, region and trust tier; longer periods beat single months; partial figures are skipped (combined lines, model families like "1/2 Series", single powertrains like i7 BEV). Germany stands in for Europe and is shown as DE.
  3. **Conflicts surfaced**: where BMW's file and a comparable public full-year figure (same line, market, year; global vs the line total) differ by more than 25 %, the market is flagged instead of either figure being silently preferred (today: 5 Series US +188 %, 5 Series China −35 %).
  4. **Areas**: the sol prompt gets a compact `market_context` (shares, trends, conflicts) with the rule that inferred causes are worded as assumptions and BMW figures are not relied on where they conflict; every area gets an additive `metrics.market` (markets its comments come from, BMW share, public trend, conflict flag). Existing areas get it by a no-LLM backfill (`python -m bmw_req.structure.market --backfill`); no re-run of areas.
  5. **UI**: the area inspector shows a Markets table (comments, BMW volume share, public trend with tier + source id, "≠ public" mark) with the label.
- Consequences: no new paid calls. Prioritisation/scoring (not rebuilt for the D-043 pipeline yet) can use the same weights later. Open for BMW (Q-015): is the US row US-only, and does China include the i5 LWB and imports?

- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("evet yapalım") after an audit of what the AI never reads; run order agreed with the main session · Status: accepted.
- Context: contextualize's evidence linking (D-043 step 4) only considered `source_item.kind = 'research'`. The web-agent findings (`web`, 138 visible) and the reference layer (`reference`, 88 visible: competitor features, trends, market facts) were never candidates, although they are cited sources of exactly the competitor / trend kind the links need.
- Decision:
  1. `node_texts` / `visible_nodes` include kinds `research`, `web` and `reference` as node type "research" (one source_item id space; the item's kind stays on `source_item` for provenance, so the evidence counts, inspector and theme views work unchanged; 3D arcs skip items without a ring position). Nearest research candidates per theme 10 → 14 so they don't crowd out research. Undated web items stay invisible (D-041).
  2. `contextualize.relink(cp)` re-runs only step 4 as a **new** contextualize run: copies the latest completed run's insights, theme membership and non-evidence edges (belongs_to, duplicate_of, sub_need_of) and insight/theme tracks, links every theme against the current pool (one luna Flex call per theme), writes edge tracks against the parent and supersedes the old run. Never in place: a completed run's edges stay as they were (rule 6, D-041 lineage). Order: cp1, then cp2, so cp2's edge states compare against the new cp1 edges.

- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("go ahead, i agree" to the proposal: ladder with PM choosing, 1–3 requirements per area, links feed prioritization as bundles/flags/enabler credit without automatic penalties, ≤ $0.5 gap research); implemented by agents · Status: accepted · Builds on D-043 (areas), D-038 (one product decision, one metric), D-012 (future horizon), D-046 (market weights). Contract: `documents/requirement-definition.md`.
- Context: BMW's reference process step 3 asks for specification & quantification ("Range: 600 or 700 mi?", "Cooler for how many bottles?", "Seat ventilation: fast enough?"), grouped by Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver assistance. `elicit.py` (never run) had metric names but no values, no acceptance criteria, no benchmarks and no links; cited numbers existed only as free text.
- Decision:
  1. **Areas are BMW's step 2** ("potential requirements, 0/1"); the new layer drafts **1–3 requirements per non-quality area** (`define`, sol), each one product decision.
  2. **`specify`**: one customer-experienced metric (no component specs — scope), ≤ 4 acceptance criteria with market conditions, and a **target ladder per line × market**: baseline (today's BMW) → threshold (competitive parity) → target (projected to launch) → stretch (delighter). The AI recommends a rung; **the PM chooses** (append-only `def_choice` + audit).
  3. **`benchmarks`**: a `spec_fact` table of cited numeric facts (attribute, value, unit, cycle, entity, source) extracted with luna from research / web / reference items, plus one capped gap-research round (≤ $0.5). Links are proposals; the PM confirms/removes/adds (`def_link_review`). Relational table, no graph DB (D-017).
  5. **Domains and car zones are config** derived from aspects (`definition/domains.py`), never chosen by the LLM; zone `underfloor` (battery & energy) added to `car_zones.ZONES`.
  6. **Prioritization (next layer)** uses links as bundles (strong components prioritized together), conflict flags between Musts ("choose ladder levels jointly") and enabler credit — no automatic score penalties from conflicts.
  7. **Page 3 "Definition"**: requirement pins on the 3D car by zone, coloured by domain; selecting one flies to its zone and shows the ladder; links are drawn as arcs through the car labelled with the via.
- Consequences: planned spend ≈ $3–4 for both checkpoints (pilot first). The old `requirement` tables stay for history. Open: scoring rebuild on `def_requirement` (prioritization layer).

# Product
<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->
## Platform
web
## Stack
React + TypeScript (Vite) frontend with three.js via react-three-fiber for real-time 3D; a small FastAPI JSON layer (`api/`) over the existing Python pipeline (`src/bmw_req`, SQLite). Chosen by Atahan on 2026-10-11 to replace the Streamlit UI (D-039). Runs locally only (confidential BMW data, AGENTS rule 1).
## Users
- **Primary: a BMW product manager (PM)** responsible for what the successor of a car line (1, 5, 7 Series) offers its customers in each market. Over a ~2-year process they review AI-drafted customer requirements, decide (approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge, always with a reason), set priorities per car × market, and hand the result to engineering — while new evidence keeps arriving.
- **Demo audience: BMW judges and mentors** of the "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon, watching the PM (Atahan) work the tool live on a laptop or projector. The UI is tuned demo-first: the story must land in a few clicks, without breaking the real tool underneath.
## Product Purpose
Turn ~10k customer comments, a customer study, sales data, option lists and cited web research into prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements for successor BMW cars, per car and market. The AI reads, groups, drafts, checks fit and scores; the PM decides; everything is traceable to the customer's words and audited. Success: a PM trusts and acts on the ranking because every number explains itself, and the judges see a living decision process, not a one-shot list.
## Positioning
Not a feedback dashboard and not a chatbot: a decision instrument. Every requirement is a product decision BMW could take or trade off, scored per market with a visible factor breakdown, traced down to individual comments, gated by brand fit, and re-proposed — never silently changed — as new evidence arrives in waves.
## Operating Context
- Simulated ~2-year process: three evidence waves (feedback has no dates), each re-scoring and producing AI change proposals the PM accepts or rejects.
- Portfolio: F70 (1 Series), G60 (5 Series), G68 (5 Series LWB, China), G70 (7 Series); markets USA, Europe, China, Rest of world.
- Hand-offs: defect-type pain goes to a Quality hand-over list, not into requirements; the approved list is exported.
- Today's car matters as a reference: the current car and its equipment (German price list; public BMW configurator) are the baseline the successor improves on.
## Capabilities and Constraints
- AI only proposes; approved/rejected/deferred need a named human and a rationale. Brand-fit FAIL blocks approval unless the PM overrides with a reason. Audit is append-only.
- Scope: customer-facing requirements only — no regulatory, engineering specs or pricing.
- Evidence and assumption are always shown apart; conflicting evidence is surfaced, not hidden; markets without own comments are labelled.
- OpenAI is the only LLM provider; $100 total budget; running a wave costs money and takes minutes.
- Terminology to keep (English): Must / Should / Could; "5 Series · USA"; Strong / Good / Limited evidence / Assumption only; Expected / Differentiator / Delighter; To review / Challenged / Approved / Deferred / Rejected; "AI suggests" for unconfirmed priorities.
- A parallel workstream (D-040+) adds requirement origins (competitors, trends, regulation, personas), a regulatory radar, customer & model groups, an offering matrix per market and market intelligence; the IA must have a home for these.
## Brand Commitments
- English UI, current domain terms.
- Dark theme only.
- A BMW-like blue accent is wanted.
- No BMW logo or trademark branding in the UI; neutral product name.
## Evidence on Hand
- Live demo database `data/app.db` (39 requirements, 151 car × market targets, 3 runs, ~1.6k audit events, findings, signals with verbatim quotes, study metrics, sales, option lists, 219 cited web items). Verbatims are BMW-confidential: localhost only.
- 3D models of today's cars: public CC BY Sketchfab models (attribution required), downloaded by Atahan into `data/models/` (Q-025). Fan-made approximations, not BMW CAD.
- No testimonials, user research or production usage exist — never fabricate them.
## Product Principles
1. The PM decides, the AI explains — every AI output is a proposal with its cause visible.
2. One number, fully opened — any score can be unfolded to its factors and down to the customer's words.
3. Markets are different customers — never average them away; show where they disagree.
4. The car is the canvas — requirements are about a physical product; show them on it.

# Design System: SharkSight

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "Track-While-Scan"**

The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. Everythin

Density sits in the contacts, not in the text. Numerals carry the information, set wide, light and tabular like instrument readouts; words are short labels. The only running text is the customer's own words, shown in the inspector at reading size. Colour is categorical and earned: each raw data type

Motion is a single event, not ambience. The volume never turns by itself; it moves only when the PM drags it. The sweep plays once on arrival and once on each checkpoint change, and contacts it passes flare white as they are acquired.

**Key Characteristics:**
- True black ground (#000) with the live 3D canvas full-bleed behind every overlay.
- Overlays pinned to the 24px edge: readout with the filter chips under it top-left, checkpoint timeline bottom-right (both frameless), inspector top-right (frameless feathered field).
- Wide, light, tabular numerals as the primary text.
- Five categorical data-type hues, one sweep blue, amber reserved for loss.
- Mark shape encodes track state: dot = held, ring = acquired by this sweep.
- One sweep per checkpoint change; no idle motion of the volume.

## Colors

A black instrument field with white ink, five categorical data hues validated on black, and two reserved signals: sweep blue and loss amber.

### Primary
- **Sweep Blue** (sweep, sweep-hi, sweep-wash): the sweep and the PM's position. The deep step colours the sweep blade's additive wash; the bright step draws the blade's leading edge, the active checkpoint node (with a 4px sweep-wash halo), the border of a filter chip in use, a chosen filter value's

### Secondary
- **Loss Amber** (lost-amber): reserved for weakened and lost tracks, which appear from the clustering stage on. Raw sources are only ever acquired, so the scan surface uses amber only for the failed-scan message (a lost signal).

### Tertiary (categorical, one hue per raw data type)
- **Comment Blue** (type-comment): customer verbatims, the galaxy at the centre of the volume.
- **Research Vermilion** (type-research): cited web research on the dated outer ring.
- **Study Aqua** (type-study): customer-study ticks on the innermost range ring.
- **Option Ochre** (type-option): price-list equipment on the options ring.
- **Sales Magenta** (type-sales): BMW sales volumes on the sales ring; forecasts render as wireframe outlines in the same hue.

The same hue colours the data type's inline legend glyph wherever the type is named (readout, ring name tags, inspector header).

### Neutral
- **Void** (void): the page and the WebGL clear colour. Never a near-black; pure black is what makes the contacts read as emitters.
- **Smoked Glass** (glass): the page switch, with a backdrop blur over the canvas.
- **Field** (field): every other panel (inspector, hover card, filter values, audit trail, dock). Plain black at 86%, under a 10px blur and a feathered edge. No glow.
- **Hairline** (hair) and **Strong Hairline** (hair-strong): panel borders, chip outlines, filter bar tracks, the checkpoint rail, the z-bar midline, scrollbars, mobile pill outlines.
- **Ink** (ink): numerals, titles, the customer quote, active labels, the held mark.
- **Ink 2** (ink-2): secondary values, filter names and counts, ring labels, the checkpoint fill.
- **Ink 3** (ink-3): micro labels, inactive tabs and nodes, meta lines. Holds at least 4.5:1 on black; it is the floor for any text.

In 3D, range rings are white at 10% opacity and the time ring is a white dashed line at 22%.

### Named Rules
**The One Blue Rule.** Sweep blue means "the sweep, or where the PM is right now". It never fills a data series and never decorates.

**The Amber Is Loss Rule.** Amber appears only for weakened or lost tracks and lost signal. Option Ochre sits near it in hue, so a lost track always also carries its cross mark; amber never encodes state on its own.

**The White Is Attention Rule.** Contacts rest in their data-type hue. They turn white only while a sweep flares them, while hovered, or under the white lock reticle. Blue is not used for hover.

## Typography

**Display Font:** Mona Sans Variable with its width axis (fallback ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif)
**Body Font:** the same family; one family runs the whole system.

**Character:** One grotesque in two voices. Numerals are stretched wide (118%), light (300) and tabular, so counts read like instrument dials; labels are the same face at normal width, small and quiet. Tabular figures are on globally.

### Hierarchy
- **Instrument** (300, 34px, line-height 1, -0.02em, width 118%): the readout totals (28px), the inspector's key figure (34px) and the checkpoint timeline's track counts (20px). Readout drops to 22px under 760px.
- **Read** (400, 18px, line-height 1.5, max 60ch): the customer's words in the inspector; the only reading text in the system.
- **Title** (500, 18px, line-height 1.35, balanced wrap): the inspected item's name or headline.
- **Body** (400, 14px, line-height 1.45): the base size; sweep-control track counts, secondary figures.
- **Detail** (400, 13px): hover-card text (clamped to three lines), inspector fact values, the source link.
- **Label** (400 or 600, 12px): filter chips, filter values and counts, layer names, "+n" increments. At 600 with 0.08em tracking it names checkpoints (JAN 26 / JUL 26).
- **Micro** (400, 11px, 0.02em, ink-3): field and readout labels, legend names, ring sublabels; at 600 with 0.1em tracking it labels the time ring.

### Named Rules
**The Numeral Leads Rule.** Where a value exists, the numeral is the largest thing in its group and its label sits beside or above it at micro size. Labels never outrank figures.

- **Sales Magenta** (type-sales): BMW sales volumes on the sales ring; forecasts render as wireframe outlines in the same hue.

The same hue colours the data type's inline legend glyph wherever the type is named (readout, ring name tags, inspector header).

### Neutral
- **Void** (void): the page and the WebGL clear colour. Never a near-black; pure black is what makes the contacts read as emitters.
- **Smoked Glass** (glass): the page switch, with a backdrop blur over the canvas.
- **Field** (field): every other panel (inspector, hover card, filter values, audit trail, dock). Plain black at 86%, under a 10px blur and a feathered edge. No glow.
- **Hairline** (hair) and **Strong Hairline** (hair-strong): panel borders, chip outlines, filter bar tracks, the checkpoint rail, the z-bar midline, scrollbars, mobile pill outlines.
- **Ink** (ink): numerals, titles, the customer quote, active labels, the held mark.
- **Ink 2** (ink-2): secondary values, filter names and counts, ring labels, the checkpoint fill.
- **Ink 3** (ink-3): micro labels, inactive tabs and nodes, meta lines. Holds at least 4.5:1 on black; it is the floor for any text.

In 3D, range rings are white at 10% opacity and the time ring is a white dashed line at 22%.

### Named Rules
**The One Blue Rule.** Sweep blue means "the sweep, or where the PM is right now". It never fills a data series and never decorates.

**The Amber Is Loss Rule.** Amber appears only for weakened or lost tracks and lost signal. Option Ochre sits near it in hue, so a lost track always also carries its cross mark; amber never encodes state on its own.

**The White Is Attention Rule.** Contacts rest in their data-type hue. They turn white only while a sweep flares them, while hovered, or under the white lock reticle. Blue is not used for hover.

## Typography

**Display Font:** Mona Sans Variable with its width axis (fallback ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif)
**Body Font:** the same family; one family runs the whole system.

**Character:** One grotesque in two voices. Numerals are stretched wide (118%), light (300) and tabular, so counts read like instrument dials; labels are the same face at normal width, small and quiet. Tabular figures are on globally.

### Hierarchy
- **Instrument** (300, 34px, line-height 1, -0.02em, width 118%): the readout totals (28px), the inspector's key figure (34px) and the checkpoint timeline's track counts (20px). Readout drops to 22px under 760px.
- **Read** (400, 18px, line-height 1.5, max 60ch): the customer's words in the inspector; the only reading text in the system.
- **Title** (500, 18px, line-height 1.35, balanced wrap): the inspected item's name or headline.
- **Body** (400, 14px, line-height 1.45): the base size; sweep-control track counts, secondary figures.
- **Detail** (400, 13px): hover-card text (clamped to three lines), inspector fact values, the source link.
- **Label** (400 or 600, 12px): filter chips, filter values and counts, layer names, "+n" increments. At 600 with 0.08em tracking it names checkpoints (JAN 26 / JUL 26).
- **Micro** (400, 11px, 0.02em, ink-3): field and readout labels, legend names, ring sublabels; at 600 with 0.1em tracking it labels the time ring.

### Named Rules
**The Numeral Leads Rule.** Where a value exists, the numeral is the largest thing in its group and its label sits beside or above it at micro size. Labels never outrank figures.

Smaller kidneys. Sharper foresight.

An AI decision instrument that turns customer voice, BMW data and cited web research into measurable, evidence-linked requirements for the next BMW. The PM decides.

The problem

10,000 customer comments. Four markets. One question: what must the successor do?

  • Evidence is scattered: verbatims, a customer study, sales and option lists, plus a fast-moving market.
  • Markets are different customers: US, Europe, China and RoW must not be averaged away.
  • It is a 2-year process: new evidence keeps arriving, and every decision has to stay traceable.
Evidence→Structure→Definition→PM decision

Every source in one 3D scan, on two real checkpoints.

& sales rows

with URL, date, trust tier
JAN · JUL2026 checkpoints;

  • Honest sales: an agent checked BMW's sales file against public figures. BMW volumes count only as a labelled weight, trends come from cited data, and gaps over 25 % are flagged.

The AI reads every comment and builds an evidence graph.

Classify→Cluster→Contextualize→Requirement areas
~45shared aspects across
all sources
562need clusters,
portfolio-wide
8,978evidence links: supports,
contradicts, competes with
37 → 41requirement areas,
JAN → JUL
  • Change is tested statistically, so new data can't fake a trend. Defects go to Quality, not into requirements.

Targetprojected to launch
Stretchdelighter
  • 76 requirements, each with one metric the customer experiences and a target ladder per car × market. The AI recommends a rung; the PM picks.
  • Every number has a basis: cited, projected, assumption or gap, drawn from 246 cited benchmarks. The AI never fills a gap with an invented number.
  • 73 links between requirements, like the roof of a House of Quality. Example: range ↔ agility, via mass.

The AI proposes. The PM decides. Everything is on record.

# SharkSight — 3-minute pitch script

Open `pitch/index.html` in a browser. Use → / Space or click to advance, ← to go back, and `f` for fullscreen.
Target: about 420 spoken words, which is about 2:50. Times are cumulative.

Figures come from `data/app.db` and `foundation/` on 2026-10-11. Re-check them before the pitch, because Definition at JUL is still being generated.

---

**1 · Title (0:00–0:15)**
This is SharkSight. The shark nose is coming back with the Neue Klasse, and we pair it with foresight. Smaller kidneys, sharper foresight. SharkSight helps a BMW product manager decide what the next car must do for its customers.

**2 · Problem (0:15–0:40)**
A PM has more than ten thousand customer comments, a customer study, sales and option lists, and a market that changes every month. US, European and Chinese customers want different things. The process runs for about two years, so every decision has to stay traceable. Our app moves from evidence to structure to definition, and the PM decides at every step.

**3 · Evidence (0:40–1:05)**
Page one shows every source as one 3D scan. It holds 10,128 comments across the 1, 5 and 7 Series, BMW's study, options and sales, and almost 1,400 cited web items with a URL, a date and a trust tier. Time runs on two real checkpoints, January and July 2026, and July builds on January. We also check BMW's own sales file against public figures. When they disagree by more than 25 %, we flag the gap instead of hiding it.

**4 · Structure (1:05–1:35)**
Page two is where the AI reads. It classifies every comment into about 45 shared aspects and clusters them into 562 needs across the portfolio. Then it links those needs to research, study and competitor evidence, about nine thousand links in total. The result is about 40 requirement areas. When new data arrives, the app tests every change for statistical significance, so noise doesn't look like a trend. Defects go to Quality, not into requirements.

**5 · Definition (1:35–2:10)**
Page three answers BMW's question: "Range: 600 or 700 miles?" Each area becomes measurable requirements, 76 so far. Each one gets a metric the customer actually experiences and a target ladder for each car and market: today's BMW, rival parity, a target projected to launch, and a stretch goal. Every number is marked as cited, projected, an assumption or a gap. The numbers come from 246 cited benchmarks, and the AI never invents one. The AI recommends a rung, and the PM picks it. The requirements are linked like the roof of a House of Quality. For example, range and agility compete through mass. All of it sits on the 3D car.

**6 · Trust (2:10–2:35)**
The AI only proposes; a named person decides, and every decision needs a reason. Nothing is overwritten. Each run is a new version, and all 2,193 audit events are append-only. Every requirement links to its evidence. We have spent about 11 dollars of our 100-dollar model budget, and every call is logged.

**7 · Next (2:35–2:50)**
Next comes prioritization per market. Linked requirements are bundled, and conflicts are decided together. Let me show you live.

---

## Facts behind the slides

- Sources: 10,128 feedback, 391 study, 458 options, 24 sales rows, 1,028 research, 245 web, 96 reference items (`source_item`).
- Structure: 562 clusters; 8,978 evidence edges; 37 areas at cp1, 41 at cp2 (D-043, D-046, D-047).
- Definition (D-048): 76 `def_requirement` (all with evidence ids), 73 `def_link`, 246 `spec_fact`. These are cp1 only, and cp2 is in progress. The cp1 ladders and the conflict links were being re-tuned on 2026-10-11.
- Audit: 2,193 `audit_event`. Spend: $10.95 in `llm_usage`.
- Don't claim: deployment (nothing is deployed), a brand-fit gate in the new pipeline, or prioritization (it is the next layer).

message.content: what do you mean by four markets?

content.text:
"Four markets" means the market split the app uses everywhere: **USA, Europe, China and Rest of world**. These are the market groups in BMW's data and in our scoring (see `PRODUCT.md`). It isn't four countries. Slide 2 lists them in its second bullet.

The phrase can mislead in two ways:
- **Rest of world** is a catch-all bucket, not a real market. For the 1 Series, about a third of its comments come from Japan and sit in that bucket.
- **China** has no customer comments at all. It is covered by the customer study, sales and web research. Saying "four markets" next to "10,000 comments" suggests every market has comments.

I'd change the slide 2 headline to **"10,000 customer comments. US, Europe, China and beyond. One question: what must the successor do?"** Alternatively, I could just drop the market count. Shall I make one of these changes?

İlk slaytı daha vurucu hale getirdim; senin "proper knowledge base, proper decisions" fikrini daha doğal bir İngilizceyle kullandım. Slayt artık şöyle:

> **SharkSight** (logo ile)
>
> ## Solid evidence.
> ## Sound decisions.
>
> 10,000 customer voices, BMW's data and cited web research in one knowledge base. The AI structures it. The PM decides what the next BMW must deliver.
>
> SMALLER KIDNEYS. SHARPER FORESIGHT. *(küçük mavi imza satırı)*

- **Başlık:** "Proper" yerine "Solid / Sound" kullandım; sunumda daha akıcı ve daha iddialı duruyor. İki kısa cümle olduğu için jüri ilk saniyede mesajı alıyor: sağlam kanıt, sağlam karar.
- **Alt metin:** Uzun açıklama üç kısa cümleye indi. Bilgi tabanı, AI'ın rolü ve kararı PM'in verdiği tek bakışta anlaşılıyor.
- **"Smaller kidneys. Sharper foresight.":** Bu cümle başlıktan çıktı ama silinmedi, altta imza satırı olarak duruyor.

`pitch/script.md` dosyasındaki 1. slayt konuşma metnini de buna göre güncelledim. Sayfayı yenileyip bakabilirsin. İstersen "Proper knowledge. Proper decisions." gibi senin orijinal ifadene daha yakın bir başlık da koyabilirim.

p='pitch/script.md'; s=open(p).read()

head=head.replace("Target: about 420 spoken words, which is about 2:50. Times are cumulative.\n\nFigures come from `data/app.db` and `foundation/` on 2026-10-11. Re-check them before the pitch, because Definition at JUL is still being generated.\n",
"Target: about 400 spoken words, which is about 2:45. Times are cumulative.\n\nThe pitch presents a vision, so it gives no exact counts. If a judge asks, use the facts at the end.\n")
body='''**1 · Title (0:00–0:15)**
This is SharkSight. Good product decisions need solid evidence. So we built one living knowledge base from every customer voice, BMW's own data and cited web research. The AI structures it, and the product manager decides what the next BMW must deliver.

**2 · Problem (0:15–0:40)**
A product manager faces thousands of customer comments, customer studies, sales and option lists, and a market that changes every month. Customers in the US, Europe and China want different things. These decisions live for years, so every one of them has to stay traceable. Our app moves from evidence to structure to definition, and the PM decides at every step.

**3 · Evidence (0:40–1:05)**
First, every source lives in one space: what customers say, BMW's own data, and cited research from the world, each with a source, a date and a trust level. Time is built in. Each new checkpoint builds on the one before, so you see what changed. And we are honest about data: when internal figures conflict with public ones, we show the conflict instead of hiding it.

**4 · Structure (1:05–1:35)**
Then the AI reads everything. It classifies comments, studies and research into one shared language, clusters them into customer needs, and links each need to the world: what supports it, what contradicts it, and where rivals compete. The result is a set of requirement areas. New data only counts as a trend if it is statistically real, and defects go to Quality, not into requirements.

**5 · Definition (1:35–2:10)**
Then we answer BMW's question: "Range: 600 or 700 miles?" Each area becomes measurable requirements. Each one gets a metric the customer actually feels and a target ladder for each car and market: today's BMW, rival parity, a target projected to launch, and a stretch goal. Every number is marked as cited, projected, an assumption or a gap, and the AI never invents one. The AI recommends a rung, and the PM picks it. Requirements are linked like the roof of a House of Quality. For example, range and agility compete through mass. And all of it sits on the 3D car.

**6 · Trust (2:10–2:30)**
The AI only proposes; a named person decides, and every decision needs a reason. Every requirement traces back to its evidence. Nothing is overwritten, every decision is audited, and every model call is logged with its cost.

**7 · Vision (2:30–2:45)**
Our vision is a product brain that keeps learning across every car line and market. Next comes prioritization per market, where linked requirements are bundled and conflicts are decided together. Let me show you live.

---

## Facts for questions (not on the slides)
'''
facts=s[s.index('## Facts behind the slides')+len('## Facts behind the slides\n'):]
open(p,'w').write(head+body+facts)
EOF

content.content:
# SharkSight — 3-minute pitch script

Open `pitch/index.html` in a browser. Use → / Space or click to advance, ← to go back, and `f` for fullscreen.
Target: about 400 spoken words, which is about 2:45. Times are cumulative.

The pitch presents a vision, so it gives no exact counts. If a judge asks, use the facts at the end.

---

**1 · Title (0:00–0:15)**
This is SharkSight. Good product decisions need solid evidence. So we built one living knowledge base from every customer voice, BMW's own data and cited web research. The AI structures it, and the product manager decides what the next BMW must deliver.


## Facts for questions (not on the slides)

- Sources: 10,128 feedback, 391 study, 458 options, 24 sales rows, 1,028 research, 245 web, 96 reference items (`source_item`).
- Structure: 562 clusters; 8,978 evidence edges; 37 areas at cp1, 41 at cp2 (D-043, D-046, D-047).
- Definition (D-048): 76 `def_requirement` (all with evidence ids), 73 `def_link`, 246 `spec_fact`. These are cp1 only, and cp2 is in progress. The cp1 ladders and the conflict links were being re-tuned on 2026-10-11.

lines: Every source in one space, always live.
The AI reads everything and builds an evidence graph.
From need to a measurable requirement, placed on the car.
The AI proposes. The PM decides. Everything is on record.
A product brain that keeps learning, across every car line and market.
Open `pitch/index.html` in a browser. Use → / Space or click to advance, ← to go back, and `f` for fullscreen.
-Target: about 400 spoken words, which is about 2:45. Times are cumulative.
+Target: about 420 spoken words, which is about 2:45. Times are cumulative.
The pitch presents a vision, so it gives no exact counts. If a judge asks, use the facts at the end.

This is SharkSight. Good product decisions need solid evidence. So we built a broad knowledge base from thousands of raw data points: customer voices, BMW's own data and cited web research. The AI structures it, and the product manager decides what the next BMW must deliver.
+I'm Atahan. And this is my team. They were last seen at kickoff.

A product manager faces thousands of customer comments, customer studies, sales and option lists, and a market that changes every month. Customers in the US, Europe and China want different things. These decisions live for years, so every one of them has to stay traceable. Our app moves from evidence to structure to definition, and the PM decides at every step.

First, every source lives in one space: what customers say, BMW's own data, and cited research from the world, each with a source, a date and a trust level. And it is live: new data keeps flowing in, every update builds on the last, and you always see what changed. We are also honest about data: when internal figures conflict with public ones, we show the conflict instead of hiding it.

Then the AI reads everything. It classifies comments, studies and research into one shared language, clusters them into customer needs, and links each need to the world: what supports it, what contradicts it, and where rivals compete. The result is a set of requirement areas. New data only counts as a trend if it is statistically real, and defects go to Quality, not into requirements.

Then we answer BMW's question: "Range: 600 or 700 miles?" Each area becomes measurable requirements. Each one gets a metric the customer actually feels and a target ladder for each car and market: today's BMW, rival parity, a target projected to launch, and a stretch goal. Every number is marked as cited, projected, an assumption or a gap, and the AI never invents one. The AI recommends a rung, and the PM picks it. Requirements are linked like the roof of a House of Quality. For example, range and agility compete through mass. And all of it sits on the 3D car.

The AI only proposes; a named person decides, and every decision needs a reason. Every requirement traces back to its evidence. Nothing is overwritten, every decision is audited, and every model call is logged with its cost.

Our vision is a product brain that keeps learning across every car line and market. Next comes prioritization per market, where linked requirements are bundled and conflicts are decided together. Let me show you live.

content.content:
The problem

Thousands of customer voices. Many markets. One question: what must the successor do?

  • Evidence is scattered: verbatims, customer studies, sales and option lists, plus a fast-moving market.
  • Markets are different customers: the US, Europe and China must not be averaged away.
  • Decisions live for years: new evidence keeps arriving, and every decision has to stay traceable.
Evidence→Structure→Definition→PM decision
Evidence

Every source in one space, always live.

Voicewhat customers say,
across car lines
DataBMW studies, options
and sales
Worldcited web research with
source, date and trust
Livenew data keeps flowing in;
every update builds on the last
  • Honest data: internal figures are checked against public ones, and conflicts are shown, never blended silently.
Structure

The AI reads everything and builds an evidence graph.

Classify→Cluster→Contextualize→Requirement areas
  • One shared language for comments, studies and research, across the whole portfolio.
  • Needs are linked to the world: what supports them, what contradicts them, and where rivals compete.
  • Change is tested statistically, so new data can't fake a trend. Defects go to Quality, not into requirements.
Definition

From need to a measurable requirement, placed on the car.

Baselinetoday's BMW
Thresholdrival parity
Targetprojected to launch
Stretchdelighter
  • One metric the customer feels, with a target ladder per car and market. The AI recommends a rung; the PM picks.
  • Every number has a basis: cited, projected, assumption or gap. The AI never invents a number to fill a gap.
  • Requirements are linked, like the roof of a House of Quality. Example: range ↔ agility, via mass.
Built for trust

The AI proposes. The PM decides. Everything is on record.

  • Every requirement traces back to the evidence behind it.
  • Every decision is audited, append-only, with who decided and why.
  • Nothing is overwritten: each run is a new version, linked to the one before.
  • Every model call is logged by step and cost.
The vision

A product brain that keeps learning, across every car line and market.

Next: prioritization per market, where linked requirements are bundled and conflicts are decided together.

SharkSight · Live demo →
